docs.title: Overview
docs.body:
Pages defines the screens people use and the journeys they take through them. It is useful on its own, before any code exists, and becomes the contract Code builds when Code is added.

**Start here**

1. Read the [Charter](#doc/charter) for what Pages owns and what it leaves to other layers.
2. Skim [Information](#info) to see what Pages keeps and what it shares.
3. Read the method for the work you were given: [Pages method](#doc/page-method) or [Flows method](#doc/flow-method).

Pages never writes another layer's information. It reads Design's kit as a copy and reports gaps back to Design.

docs.title: Charter
docs.body:
## Purpose

Define the pages and flows people use to complete the product's intent. A project may start directly in Pages without Vision, Design or Code.

## Contents and scope

Own page identities, the Map, page specifications and content, navigation, states, flows and review observations. Reusable tokens and component contracts belong to Design when Design exists; built behaviour belongs to the managed application.

## Quality bar

Flows are coherent and page states are explicit, accessible and reviewable. A missing neighbour is an evidence gap, not a reason to invent its outputs.

docs.title: Pages method
docs.body:
Start with a blank page or an observed route. Map the visitor's job, specify sections and states, then review the page at desktop and phone widths.

An observed Code route is evidence of current behaviour, not proof of intended UX. Ask when intent is unclear.

docs.title: Flows method
docs.body:
A flow follows one persona through one activity, step by step, naming the page each step happens on and why the person moves on.

Review a flow by walking it: each step gets a verdict, and a failed step becomes Work on the page that failed.

docs.title: Map
docs.body:
The Map lays every page out on a grid by area and depth. Drag to move a page; links between pages are drawn from each page's links.

**Edits:** [Map](#node/map).

docs.title: Pages
docs.body:
One page at a time: its sections in order, each section's component and content, and its states. Spec and Built are two views of the same page.

**Edits:** [Pages](#node/pages).

docs.title: Flows
docs.body:
A flow's steps across pages, played as a walkthrough, with review notes per step.

**Edits:** [Flows](#node/flows).

docs.title: Kit
docs.body:
The tokens, components and brand assets Pages draws with. Today they are a copy of Design's design system, so the tab is read-only and each item has **Propose a change**, which goes to Design as Work.

If the Design system binding ends, the copy becomes Pages' own and the tab becomes editable.

**Edits:** [Kit](#node/kit).

information.title: Map
information.intent: Where every page sits and how pages link, as one picture of the product.
information.body:
One map per project. Each page has a place (column, row); columns are areas of the product and rows are depth.

The map does not hold pages; it places them. Removing a page from the map does not delete the page.

information.title: Pages
information.intent: Each screen a person can reach: its route, purpose, sections, content and states.
information.body:
A page is one screen with a stable id. Its sections are ordered top to bottom; each section names the component it uses, the stories it serves, and its content.

States (empty, loading, error, signed out) are listed per page and must each be reviewable.

A page here is a **specification**. The built screen lives in Code; Code's route for this page should follow it.

fields: Name shown in nav and on the map
What the visitor comes here to do
Ordered: name, component, region, stories, content, state

information.title: Flows
information.intent: Journeys one persona takes across pages to finish one activity, with review verdicts.
information.body:
A flow names a persona and an activity, then lists steps. Each step names the page it happens on, what triggers the next step, and why.

Flows reference Vision's personas and stories by id.

information.title: Kit
information.intent: The tokens, components and brand assets pages are drawn with.
information.body:
Pages draws every page with a kit. Each kit item is a copy of something in the design system, converted by Pages' kit adapter into the shape Pages' canvas renders.

Pages does not invent kit items. A gap is reported to the layer that owns the design system.

fields: The design-system entry it was copied from
That entry's revision, to notice drift

children.title: Tokens
children.intent: Colour roles, type scale, spacing and corners.
children.body: One item per token group, as resolved values the canvas can use directly.

fields: Resolved values for light and dark

children.title: Components
children.intent: The building blocks sections are made of.
children.body: One item per component, with the props and variants Pages' sections can choose.

children.title: Brand
children.intent: The app's name, mark and imagery as pages show them.
children.body: The name, the mark (logo) and approved imagery.
